svg.title: Topological Sort
svg.desc: Topological Sort. Order tasks so every dependency comes before what needs it, as build tools and package managers do; a cycle makes it impossible. Step 1, Dependencies as a graph: An arrow means builds before; a badge counts unbuilt prerequisites. Only utils has 0, so it starts. Step 2, Build what's ready: Take the front of the queue, output it, and decrement what needs it; a badge at 0 joins the queue. Step 3, Waves run in parallel: Modules that became ready together don't need each other: 6 parallel rounds instead of 8 builds. Step 4, A cycle stops it: One new import makes users need orders: after 5 builds the queue is empty, and a cycle is reported.

g.text: An arrow means builds before; a badge counts unbuilt prerequisites. Only utils has 0, so it starts.
Take the front of the queue, output it, and decrement what needs it; a badge at 0 joins the queue.
Modules that became ready together don't need each other: 6 parallel rounds instead of 8 builds.
One new import makes users need orders: after 5 builds the queue is empty, and a cycle is reported.

text.class: mono b ts-cnt end f-red ts-kred

g.text: each module and arrow handled once
as many as the longest chain
fewer than 8 output means a cycle
api needs users, orders and logging, so its badge is 3
utils needs nothing: badge 0, so it goes straight into the ready queue
KAHN'S ALGORITHM, ONE MODULE PER LOOP
1 take the module at the front of the queue and add it to the build order
2 subtract 1 from the badge of every module that needs it
3 a module whose badge reaches 0 joins the back of the queue
a module is ready one round after its latest prerequisite, so no arrow joins two modules of one round
longest chain: utils → config → db → users → orders → api = 6 rounds
config and logging can swap: neither needs the other, so both orders are valid
new import: users now needs orders, so users waits on 3 modules
the queue is empty after 5 of 8: users and orders wait for each other, api waits on both
